subject: DONE s388b (merged 297b5e4): poisoned-`my` family deleted — enabler + 3 families; #205 closes; TOTAL +34
description:
SHIPPED s388b, merged to main at 297b5e4.  #205 closes with it.

Replayed the four s384 commits the full sweep had rejected, once all four
blockers they exposed were closed (#294 a311943, #298 a1e3814, #297 e3616eb,
#296 66bdb93).  Branch wip/s388-291, four commits, each independently gated:

 62d88e2  enabler: _forward_global_decls stops excluding _seg_lex names in
          FILE mode (`my $lb = $free_out ? ($seg_lex // {}) : {}`); EVAL mode
          keeps the exclusion, because there the list is the p-eval-thunk's
          capture PARAMETERS from the caller, not declarations.  #205 CLOSES.
          Gate 5109.
 2817d96  delete __shadow__ (nested bare block).  Gate 5110.
 9e2760d  delete __cond__ (if/while/C-for head).  Gate 5117.
 781f3f8  delete __emb__ — REPLACED BY NARROWING THE VETO.  Gate 5118.

WHY THE ENABLER IS FIRST: the renames had TWO causes and the plan named only
one.  Cause A (removed by the #290 flip): a defvar proclaims its symbol
special, so declaring a name the section also let-binds turned that `let` into
a dynamic rebind.  Cause B: _forward_global_decls SKIPS any _seg_lex name, so a
nested `my $x` cost the global $x its declaration.  Probed: deleting
_rename_poisoned_block_mys alone drops `(p-defcell @a …)` and file-level @a
crashes.

FAMILY 3 IS THE REAL FIX, not a deletion.  _lower_block's let-hoist VETO
presumes another named sub shares the forward-declared global as this decl's
cell — true at FILE level (#199), false inside a sub body (#265, #272).  s368
could not narrow it because the `let` suppressed the GLOBAL's declaration; the
enabler removed that, so the narrowing IS the fix.  11 lines added, 96 removed.

RESULT: corpus rename bindings 716/128/5 -> 36/0/0, ~345 lines out of
Parser2.pm + ExprToCL.pm.  The 36 survivors are _gate_seam_my_shadow, a v1-seam
mechanism with a live cause, gone with #153.

FULL SWEEP: GATE clean after the baseline edit — 0 new / 0 fixed, 2 unstable
(postfixderef.t, ref.t, known PARTIAL).  TOTAL passing 18498 -> 18532 (+34),
per file: closure.t +14, eval.t +13 (9 of them #296-B1's), method.t +4,
for.t +2, my.t +1.

FOUR new closure.t rows edited into docs/fail-baseline.tsv by hand with causes
(newly REACHABLE, not new breakage — the file used to die at load and drop a
whole top-level form): t264 RT #1028, t265 RT #10085, t270 (unnamed,
is($flag,1) at closure.t:653) = DESTROY at scope exit (#198); t272 'cloneable
with //ee' = an anon sub is not cloned per statement-modifier `for` iteration.

GOTCHAS WORTH KEEPING (also in DECIDED s388c/s388d):
 - A replay of reverted work is NOT a cherry-pick: every Parser2.pm hunk
   conflicted because #296's two passes now sit INSIDE families 1 and 2's
   deletion spans, sharing their comment headers.
 - Twice the s384 hunk tried to shorten _eval_lexical_alist's strip list back
   to its s384 shape and would have taken `__excl__` (#296) with the dead
   suffixes.  A suffix leaves that list only when its MINTER leaves.
 - corpus-diff carries no signal for a change like this (emission moves for
   nearly every file by construction); the sweep is the measurement.</description>
